stories.title: 'Conscience does not permit': LHC's Justice Kayani resigns, cites executive's growing control over judiciary
summary: Justice Kayani previously served as the senior puisne judge of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and was expecting to be elevated to chief justice.

However, the transfer of Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar from the LHC, along with two other judges from the Sindh and Balochistan high courts, prompted him to challenge the inter-high court transfers.

After he was transferred to the LHC’s Rawalpindi registry, the new duty roster assigned him only to a single bench despite his previous position as the IHC’s senior puisne judge and his pending challenge to the inter-high court transfers.

stories.title: Lahore again ranks world’s most polluted major city as smog worsens
summary: According to the live air quality ranking published by Swiss air quality monitoring platform IQAir, Lahore recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 296 at 10am on October 28, placing it at the top of the list of the world’s major cities.
The worsening air quality coincided with colder conditions in Lahore during the early morning, when smog reduced visibility and added to concerns over the city’s deteriorating air quality.

Lahore air quality map. —IQAir Environment Protection Agency (EPA) spokesperson Sajid Bashir told Dawn that the authorities were monitoring industries and had installed devices to record pollution levels.

stories.title: Trump tamed after US midterms? Europe doubts it
summary: President Donald Trump may be facing a political pounding at the US midterm elections next month — but in Europe expectations are low that a big Democrat win would change much.

But while the hope may be that Trump could be reined in by a hostile Congress, multiple officials at the EU and NATO told AFP they doubt a big loss would muzzle him on the international stage. “We don’t think the unpredictability is going to change,” said one senior EU diplomat.
Ukraine, tariffs Ahead of the midterms, Trump has rattled Europe by yet again lashing out at Ukraine and cosying up to Russia as Washington has renewed its push to end the fighting.

stories.title: ‘Have no illusions’: Kundi tells Afghan Taliban Pakistan will not tolerate attacks after Angoor Adda firing
summary: The incident took place on Tuesday night when Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on Pakistan Army border posts and residential areas in the Angoor Adda border area.
It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.
Around mid-October, the state media reported that security forces had again responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in KP’s Upper Kurram.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab lashes India coast, no deaths reported
summary: Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India’s southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday, but there were no initial reports of deaths, a top official said.

Cyclone Arnab hit southeastern Andhra Pradesh state as a “very severe cyclonic storm”, with winds of 115-125 kilometres (71-77 miles) per hour and gusts reaching 140 kph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an update at 0830 am (0300 GMT).
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu said there had been no reported deaths from the storm, congratulating government officers who had “worked tirelessly throughout the night”.

stories.title: Pod of bottlenose dolphins spotted off Gwadar
summary: GWADAR: A massive pod of more than 500 dolphins was spotted near a fishing boat in the coastal waters off Gwadar.

Marine experts and environmentalists have described the sighting of such a large group of dolphins as a positive indicator of abundant marine life, rich food sources and a healthy ocean ecosystem in the region.
Pakistan’s coastal waters, particularly along the Balochistan coast, are home to diverse marine life, including around 26 recorded species of cetaceans, such as dolphins, whales and porpoises.

stories.title: Netanyahu, rival Eisenkot both vow to form government after inconclusive Israeli election
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot each vowed on Wednesday to form a government after both came up short in the first election since the events of October 7, 2023.

Eisenkot, speaking to his own supporters in Tel Aviv, issued a veiled warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said.
But Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers — and Netanyahu again suggested that a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy.

stories.title: Lahore High Court rules against divorce-linked Quran oath
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court has held that an offer to settle a civil dispute through a “special oath” on the Holy Quran, coupled with a condition of divorce if the oath is false, is not a lawful offer.

During a pending appeal before an appellate court, the petitioner had offered in August 2023 to have the matter decided by an oath on the Holy Quran taken by the opposing side, with a condition that the oath-taker’s wife would stand divorced if the oath proved false.
On Aug 22, the respondents appeared before the appellate court and expressed willingness to take the oath, while the petitioner said he did not wish to proceed.

stories.title: Rawalpindi man, parents held after woman alleges torture
summary: RAWALPINDI: Police detained a man and his parents on Tuesday following a complaint by his wife, who alleged that she had been tortured in the Chaklala area.
The woman, a resident of Shah Khalid Colony, registered an FIR with Chaklala police, stating that she had been married for five years.
A police spokesperson said senior officers had taken notice of a social media post about violence against a woman in Chaklala area, and police traced the woman and her family.

stories.title: Rawalpindi traders warn of protests against Suthra Punjab sanitation tax
summary: Say they already pay property taxes, Wasa bills and other charges They stated that the monthly sanitation fees imposed on shops and commercial centres under the Clean Punjab Programme were unacceptable.

Given this, the question arises: since property tax and Wasa bills already include charges for municipal and sanitation services, why is an additional financial burden being imposed on traders through separate sanitation bills under the ‘Suthra Punjab’ (Clean Punjab) initiative?
The business community has the right to know exactly which services are being covered by property taxes, Wasa bills, and the new ‘Suthra Punjab’ charges.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court sentences man to life for killing woman
summary: PESHAWAR: Peshawar High Court has set aside acquittal of a suspect by a trial court and sentenced him to life imprisonment for killing a woman inside her house in Charsadda district over 10 years ago.

The bench convicted the suspect under Section 302 of Pakistan Penal Code for intentional murder of Ms Wajahat and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for life and also directed him to pay compensation to the tune of Rs500,000 to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The bench further convicted him for house trespassing under Section 449 of PPC and sentenced him to seven years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs200,000.

stories.title: Constitutional questions
summary: The emergency provisions enable federal rule over a province if the president is satisfied that certain conditions exist.
Could the president have refused to sign the recent emergency proclamation notwithstanding the advice of the federal government?
It is incorrect to state that because emergency powers exist in the Constitution, the exercise thereof is constitutional.

stories.title: No room for negligence in anti-terror fight: Kundi
summary: The governor commended the sacrifices made by the provincial police to maintain peace and said that the force was fighting terrorism on the frontline.

He said that steps were being taken to improve police stations, checkposts, facilities and infrastructure in the tribal districts, while armoured personnel carriers, modern weapons and other necessary equipment were being provided to the police.
The governor also said that development funds would be used to meet the provincial police’s requirements and that the federal government had already provided 10 APCs to the force.

stories.title: Two arrested for torturing transperson to death in Bahawalnagar
summary: BAHAWALNAGAR: Two suspects have been arrested for allegedly torturing a transgender person, a former victim response officer (VRO) at the Bahawalnagar DPO office, to death for refusing to withdraw a case of harassment and violence registered against them.
Explaining the motive for the animosity, police officials told Dawn that the deceased had registered a case against the suspects and she had allegedly received death threats from them.
The FIR registered with the B-Division police stated that a girl from Sadaat Colony alleged that about a year ago, she became acquainted with a Pera official during the recruitment examinations.

stories.title: Online bike rider held for harassing female passenger in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: Police claim to have traced and arrested an online bike service rider for allegedly harassing a female passenger in Johar Town area.
As per initial reports, the incident took place a few days back when the female passenger booked a ride from F-2 Johar Town.
According to the FIR, the male driver had been physically harassing the female passenger throughout the journey and she had asked him multiple times to stop the inappropriate acts.

stories.title: CM Maryam concerned at grant of bail to offender in girl’s torture case
summary: GUJRAT: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday warned offenders to stop targeting women and girls as the law would apply equally to the rich and the poor.

Urges judiciary to ensure that punishments serve as a deterrent She added that the suspects in rape cases in Punjab were being arrested within two hours, adding that the government wanted women and vulnerable citizens to feel protected by the state.
The chief minister said the government was providing students with laptops, scholarships, electric bikes and chromebooks to help them pursue education and build a better future.

stories.title: Rabies toll in Sindh rises to 43 with one more death
summary: HYDERABAD: A six-year-old boy from Badin has died of rabies at Liaquat University Hospital (LUH) despite having been given rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) and anti-rabies vaccine, bringing the number of rabies deaths in Sindh to 43 so far.
The boy, Bilal, son of Amjad Rajput, died on Oct 24 at the LUH’s city branch, according to the health department.

According to Dr Ershad Kazmi, LUH’s medical superintendent, focal person for dog-rabies cases and head of the hospital’s rabies prevention centre, Bilal was bitten by a dog on Sept 29 in Goth Bachal Balan.

stories.title: The Tehran opening
summary: Against that backdrop, the visit by senior Saudi officials to Tehran stands out as a significant outreach at a time of profound tension between the two countries, with Saudi Arabia absorbing near-daily attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis.

For Iran, the presence of senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan has been symbolically important: Iranian officials are eager to sideline the US from regional security and diplomatic arrangements.

For all the positivity, the central question remains whether the meeting could bridge the gap and help prevent a new round of US-Israeli aggression against Iran and, more importantly, de-escalate the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

stories.title: UN agency highlights ‘complex’ water management of Sindh
summary: The report advised the Sindh government to take careful stock of its land and water resources, including all available water sources such as rainfall, groundwater, canal diversions, lakes, reservoirs and direct rivers.

The report presented an analytical framework for sector-level water accounting using on-the-ground data, and offered a comprehensive assessment of the demand and supply sides, which needs to be discussed, improved and used in decision-making.
Official reports on water use in rain-fed and well-irrigated areas are often contradictory.

stories.title: Regional security
summary: THE fact that high officials from the Makkah defence pact partner states — Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — were in Tehran on Monday made global headlines, and with good reason.
All regional states are wary of possible fresh US/Israeli attacks on Iran, and the Tehran meeting must be seen in this framework.
In fact, while inviting Iran to join the Makkah alliance may not be practical at this juncture, regional states can at least agree to a common non-aggression framework.

stories.title: Balochistan doctors to go on strike from Nov 1
summary: The decision was taken at a joint meeting of various doctors’ organisations chaired by PMA General Secretary Dr Zarak Muhammad Shahi.
Participants discussed the planned strike and other key issues concerning the provincial health department.

stories.title: Three cops injured in attack on Khuzdar DIG convoy
summary: KHUZDAR/ DERA MURAD JAMALI: Three police personnel were injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on the convoy of Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Khuzdar Range Imran Qureshi and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Khuzdar in Karkh tehsil.
As the convoy was returning, armed men, lying in ambush, opened fire on it, injuring three police personnel.
According to Noshki police, armed men opened fire at the girls’ college, injuring three students.

stories.title: Delay in compensation for seafarers’ families alarms Senate committee
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate Functio­nal Committee on Human Rights on Tuesday expressed concern over delays in compensation to families of Pakistani seafarers affected by a hostage-taking incident off Somalia.

Taking up the case of Pakistani seafarers, the committee sought explanations from officials over delays in the crew’s release, repatriation of a deceased seafarer’s body, medical treatment for injured crew members and financial assistance to affected families.
The chairperson stressed that insurance-related procedures and disputes among the parties concerned should not cause unnecessary delays in payments to affected families.

stories.title: India deploys extra forces after protests against dam
summary: GUWAHATI: India has deployed hundreds of additional security personnel in its remote northeast, authorities said on Tuesday, after youth protesters clashed with police last week over a plan to build a mega-dam to counter a Chinese hydropower project upstream.
Protests in Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang Valley, which borders Tibet, turned violent last week, triggering clashes with police, who made at least 21 arrests.
The Siang river flows into Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Zangbo.

stories.title: Pakistan warns against escalation in Iran crisis, urges diplomacy
summary: WASHINGTON: Pakistan has warned that the situation surrounding Iran’s nuclear programme has sharply deteriorated, urging all sides to exercise restraint and resolve the dispute through diplomacy amid continued hostilities and divisions within the UN Security Council.
The dispute centres on international concerns over Iran’s nuclear activities and the verification of its commitments under the non-proliferation regime.
The Pakistani envoy highlighted Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to promote de-escalation, a ceasefire and negotiations.

stories.title: Lahore High Court Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani resigns
summary: Justice Kayani had been transferred from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in May this year and had been performing his duties at the LHC principal seat.

In April this year, the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) approved the transfer of Kayani to the LHC, Justice Babar Sattar to the Peshawar High Court (PHC) and Justice Saman Riffat Imtiaz to the Sindh High Court (SHC).

In February 2025, when Justice Sardar Sarfraz Dogar was elevated to the position of IHC chief justice from the LHC, the same three judges were among a group of five who refused to accept his elevation.

stories.title: Haris reprimanded, England fined after Lahore ODI
summary: Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has been reprimanded and fined 20 per cent of his match fee for breaching the International Cricket Council's (ICC) Code of Conduct during Sunday's one-day international against England in Lahore, the governing body said on Wednesday.
The incident occurred at the end of the 46th over of Pakistan's innings when Haris, at the non-striker's end, appealed for a wide before arguing with England all-rounder Will Jacks.
Under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl within the allotted time.

stories.title: Nine terrorists killed in two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan: ISPR
summary: Security forces killed nine terrorists belonging to Indian backed Fitna al-Hindustan during two Intelligence-Based Operations (IBOs) in Balochistan's Kachhi and Wadh districts, the military's media wing said on Wednesday.

In the first operation in Kachhi district, security forces targeted a terrorist hideout, resulting in an intense exchange of fire. “After an intense fire exchange, seven Indian sponsored terrorists were sent to hell,” ISPR said.

On October 23, Security forces killed 10 terrorists, including a woman, during operations in Gwadar after Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists attempted attacks near the Gabd border crossing and in Gwadar city, the military’s media wing said.

stories.title: Karachi court reserves verdict on journalist Iqrarul Hassan's bail plea in PECA case
summary: Karachi's District and Sessions Court (East) on Wednesday reserved its verdict on journalist Iqrarul Hassan's bail application in a case for harming the state and national integrity by disseminating anti-state content on his social media platforms.

On October 13, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) produced Hassan before the judicial magistrate (East) at Karachi's city court and he was handed over to the NCCIA on a four-day physical remand.

Later, on October 16, the District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters.

stories.title: Policeman martyred in North Waziristan attack
summary: NORTH WAZIRISTAN: A police constable was martyred when unidentified assailants opened fire on him in Eidak Bazaar in Mirali tehsil here on Tuesday afternoon, police said.
They said that the incident took place at around 4pm when unidentified assailants opened fire on Asmatullah in the bazaar, killing him on the spot.
A contingent of police reached the site after receiving information about the incident.

stories.title: Absence of bridges over river adds to misery of upper Bara residents
summary: Saddam Khan, a schoolteacher in Dray Wandi village of Sipah area, told this scribe that he had to take his ailing wife to a health centre in Paindi area, some 15km from his home on his shoulders while crossing the river on foot at nighttime.

Haji Hashmat, a resident of Dray Wandi, urged authorities to fix the steel bridge of Saukh village somewhere in Sipah area as the government had started constructing a concrete bridge at the same location in Saukh.
He said that shifting of the steel bridge from Saukh to Sipah would benefit nearly 4,000 families of Sipah, Zakhakhel, Kamarkhel and Qambarkhel tribes, residing on the ‘wrong’ side of the Bara River.

stories.title: 1,500 prisoners to be shifted to Islamabad Model Jail in first phase: Naqvi
summary: Talking to media at the newly-built Islamabad Model Jail at H-16, Mr Naqvi, accompanied by State Minister for Interior Talal Chaudhry, said the jail project had been completed and would be inaugurated within “two to four days” by the prime minister.
The minister gave credit to the State Minister Talal Chaudhry and the CDA chairman and his team for the early completion of the jail project.
The minister said if construction continued at the current pace, the project could be completed in less than 30 days.

stories.title: Half of key Pera positions lying vacant in Pindi
summary: The meeting included a detailed review of Pera’s performance in the Rawalpindi district, covering areas such as price control, anti-encroachment efforts, the resolution of public grievances, and progress on the establishment of enforcement stations.

Similarly, 226 inspections were conducted to address activities causing public nuisance or grievances; this resulted in the issuance of 175 challans and the imposition of Rs1.9 million in fines, while 66 premises were sealed.
The meeting also reviewed progress on the establishment of enforcement stations across the district’s seven tehsils.
